source.title: Toy Models of Feature Absorption in SAEs

record.tranche_reason: The post reports toy-model experiments showing feature absorption under co-occurrence and how its extent changes with sparsity penalty and tied weights, refining the claim that feature splitting is clean.
record.gate_note: The post tests absorption in toy SAEs, not dictionary-size scaling or nested feature families. Its discussion of Gemma Scope results and other cited work is background, not a new result here. The sample firing-pattern tables are flattened in the supplied text, but their feature columns and sample rows are identifiable.
record.test_reason: Toy SAE experiments with controlled feature co-occurrence show absorption. Feature 1 fires only when feature 0 fires, so it is a hierarchical parent/child setup. The experiments also show how absorption varies with magnitude variance, L1 penalty and tied weights. This bears directly on V4, and on V6's claim that the training objective produces the effect. This LessWrong post is not one of the original sources, although its author co-wrote 'A is for Absorption'.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author shows in toy models that co-occurrence causes absorption, which he frames as a sparsity-maximising strategy of the SAE. Magnitude variance gives partial absorption, and higher L1 increases absorption under imperfect co-occurrence. Tying encoder and decoder weights fixes absorption in the toy setups but raises MSE, and it is untested on non-toy SAEs. The author also argues absorption will occur wherever features co-occur, which he calls the norm.
record.recipe_differences: Uses controlled toy feature firing patterns and SAE training to investigate absorption, rather than training SAEs of increasing dictionary size and matching coarse features to finer features.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature co-occurrence and its imperfectness, feature-magnitude variation, L1 coefficient, superposition, and whether encoder and decoder weights are tied.
record.problems: The reported experiments are controlled toy models; the author explicitly says tied weights have not been tested on a non-toy SAE. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The tied-weight superposition result has a higher MSE than the pre-superposition result, but no numerical loss is given.

untested.parts: SAE dictionary size is not varied. Sparsity is varied only via L1 under imperfect co-occurrence. No real-model SAEs are trained in this post (Gemma Scope findings are cited background).
No Matryoshka SAEs and no real-model features. The post does not test whether absorption tells us anything about the model's own units.
Not tested: no nested feature families or their geometry.
Not tested: no comparison of latents across dictionary sizes.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 untested note says hierarchy was not tested. That is wrong: feature 1 fires only when feature 0 fires, which is a parent/child structure. I re-labelled the tied-weight results from 'challenges' to 'limits_scope' for V4, because V4's 'doesn't fix it' clause concerns size and sparsity, not weight tying. For V6 I re-labelled them to 'supports', because V6 explicitly says changed objectives can alter the effect. All results are toy-only, with no uncertainty estimates. Commenters note that tied weights reduce sparsity on real problems, which is not tested here.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over SAE dictionary size or test of whether larger dictionaries replace coarse features with several finer features.
No large-model or open-SAE-release test; the reported experiments use toy networks.
No test of nested feature families or whether they mirror a hierarchy of concepts.
The toy experiments test absorption under feature co-occurrence, but not whether the features are hierarchical, nor whether changing SAE dictionary size fixes absorption.
No comparison of larger- and smaller-SAE latents or test for novel latents across dictionary sizes.

Tests L1 sparsity penalties and tied encoder/decoder weights on toy inputs; does not test Matryoshka SAEs, real-model features, or whether the result establishes what units the model itself represents.

relation.reason: The toy experiments bear directly on whether absorption occurs and when.

tranche.reason: Gives results that V4 is partial or needs restating: partial absorption with a weakly firing parent, L1-dependent absorption under imperfect co-occurrence, and tied weights removing it. It also argues that splitting into absorbed latents is a co-occurrence/sparsity artifact.

source_check.notes: LessWrong post by chanind, an author of the absorption paper; no peer review; Colab code. The tied-weight results come from plots only, with no MSE number. The setup states L1 3e-5, yet the 95% section raises L1 'from 5e-3'. The flattened sample tables can be parsed, but the latent order differs between runs.

statements.correction: Tied weights remove absorption in the 4-feature and 10-feature toys (r7, r9). MSE is 'no longer 0' only in the 10-feature superposition toy, with no number given. Tying is untested on non-toy SAEs.
statements.problem: Attaches an MSE cost to both toys. The text reports a cost only for the 10-feature superposition tied SAE and implies MSE was 0 before superposition.

statements.correction: At 95% co-occurrence: partial absorption at L1 5e-3 (r5), where the parent latent fires with reduced magnitude. At L1 2e-2 the parent latent fails to fire when both are active (r6).
statements.problem: Says 95% co-occurrence gives partial absorption but omits the L1 condition. The study's point is that imperfect co-occurrence still gives full absorption at a higher L1.

statements.correction: Independent: no absorption (r1). Perfect co-occurrence: parent hole (r2). 95% co-occurrence: reduced absorption at L1 5e-3 (r5), but the parent latent fails to fire at L1 2e-2 (r6).
statements.problem: Says 95% co-occurrence gives reduced absorption with no L1 condition. That holds only at L1 5e-3; at 2e-2 absorption is full.
